capabilities: record command executions from hotkeys and the command palette
show per-command usage counts, daily counts, and last-use dates in a dedicated view
identify frequently used commands to assign hotkeys and rarely used ones to free up hotkeys
limit recorded data by maximum record count and retention period
extras: Only executions via hotkeys or the command palette are tracked; ribbon and UI-triggered commands are not. Recorded data (stored in IndexedDB) is deleted when the plugin is updated, disabled, or uninstalled unless protected in desktop settings; old records are also dropped past a configurable count (default 2000) or retention period (default 60 days). README lists known bugs where hotkeys fail to appear in the table after restart.
problem: Obsidian gives no visibility into which commands you actually use, so deciding which commands deserve hotkeys or which plugins to uninstall is guesswork.
summary: Command usage tracker that records how many times each command runs and shows counts and last-use dates in a view.
